Here is the issue description:
# CV-X-IF vs. CORE-V-XIF
In https://github.com/openhwgroup/core-v-xif/pull/124/commits/8d7a432ceaca51b62af772b449af29e26120ad02 the term `CORE-V-XIF` is replaced by `CV-X-IF` in `README.md` and `intro.rst` files.
Is there any reason to keep `CORE-V-XIF` in `x_ext.rst` file? For the sake of consistency, it would be preferable to use only one acronym.

Here is the project file that may be relevant to this issue: README.md 1 # OpenHW Group Specification: Core-V eXtension interface (CV-X-IF) 2 3 The Core-V eXtension interface (CV-X-IF) is a RISC-V eXtension interface that provides a generalized framework suitable to implement custom coprocessors and ISA extensions for existing RISC-V processors. 4 5 It features independent channels for accelerator-agnostic offloading of instructions and writeback of the result(s). 6 7 ## Documentation 8 9 The CV-X-IF user manual can be found in the _docs_ folder and it is 10 captured in reStructuredText, rendered to html using [Sphinx](https://docs.readthedocs.io/en/stable/intro/getting-started-with-sphinx.html). 11 These documents are viewable using readthedocs and can be viewed [here](https://docs.openhwgroup.org/projects/openhw-group-core-v-xif/). 12 13 ## Changelog 14 15 A changelog is generated automatically in the documentation from the individual pull requests. Pull requests labeled with *ignore-for-release* are ignored for the changelog generation.

Your task is to:
1. Carefully review the issue description and thoroughly analyze the issue to uncover all possible causes.
2. Review the provided code file and identify at least three locations within the file that require inspection or modification to resolve the issue.

4. Check the functionally similar or similarly named methods/classes that might have the same bug or require consistency updates.

The issue centers on inconsistent use of acronyms: in recent commits, “CORE-V-XIF” was replaced by “CV-X-IF” in README.md and intro.rst, but x_ext.rst still contains the old acronym. To resolve this and maintain consistency, we need to verify that every occurrence or reference to the old name/acronym in README.md is updated to “CV-X-IF” (or otherwise justified). While the provided snippet is only 15 lines, there are at least three distinct locations where the acronym/full name appears or is implied and should be inspected or modified:

1. Title line (line 1) – the full name “Core-V eXtension interface” appears alongside the acronym; decide whether to shorten or rephrase.
2. Introductory sentence (line 3) – repeats “The Core-V eXtension interface (CV-X-IF)”; may be redundant or inconsistent.
3. Documentation URL and project path (lines 11–12) – the URL uses “openhw-group-core-v-xif” which, if the project acronym is being standardized to CV-X-IF, may need updating or at least a comment.

By targeting these locations, we ensure that the README.md fully aligns with the desired “CV-X-IF” branding and help prevent similar oversights in related rst files.
